title: Scenario 00 in Ring Topology
description: This scenario explores scenario 00 dynamics within a ring communication topology. The ring topology limits information flow to immediate neighbors, creating latency and potential misinformation cascades. This tests the agents' ability to coordinate freight movement using only local information and indirect communication.
edge_cases_to_watch: Information lag due to ring hop latency
Conflicting instructions from distant agents relayed through neighbors
Congestion at single-capacity routes (east-north) caused by indirect coordination failures
Deadlocks where agents wait for information that is circulating in the wrong direction
coordination_challenges: Multi-hop information decay: Messages losing accuracy as they pass through neighbors
Global state estimation: Agents must infer the state of the whole system using only local neighbor updates
Split-brain scenarios: Agents on opposite sides of the ring forming divergent coordination plans
suggested_agent_strategies: Gossip-based consensus: Periodically relaying neighbor state to increase global awareness
Predictive routing: Using historical turn data to anticipate depot congestion without direct communication
Redundancy injection: Sending high-priority job status updates in both directions (clockwise and counter-clockwise)
success_criteria: Agents maintain a consistent global state estimate despite topology constraints
Minimal throughput loss compared to a fully-connected communication graph
